title: Notifications
description: Approvals, request updates and announcements meant for you, newest first.

empty.allBody: When something needs your attention — an approval, an update on your request or a new announcement — it shows up here.
empty.unreadBody: There's nothing new since you last looked.

admin.title: Notification delivery
admin.description: Besides the in-app inbox, notifications can go out by email and to Microsoft Teams, Slack or your own systems.
admin.copyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select the text and copy it manually.

channels.intro: Post selected notifications to a team channel or another system — for example escalations to the IS on-call channel. Messages are written in the channel's language.
channels.emptyBody: Connect a Microsoft Teams or Slack channel, or any HTTPS endpoint, to receive selected notifications.
channels.deleteBody: Notifications stop going to this channel right away. Its delivery history stays in the log.

test.hint: Post a test message now, even while the channel is off
test.sent: Test message delivered. Check the channel.
test.failed: The channel didn't accept the test message.

form.createDescription: Choose where messages go and which notifications to send there.
form.editDescription: Change the name, language or notifications. Leave the URL empty to keep the current one.

guide.teams: In Microsoft Teams, open the channel, choose ••• › Workflows › “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”, finish the steps and copy the URL it shows.
guide.slack: In Slack, create an app at api.slack.com/apps, turn on Incoming Webhooks, choose “Add New Webhook to Workspace”, pick the channel and copy the URL (https://hooks.slack.com/services/…).
guide.webhook: Any HTTPS endpoint you run. We POST JSON with the title, body, link and type, signed with a secret you get once after saving, so you can check each request really comes from us.

form.name: Name
form.urlKeepPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the current URL
form.urlKeep: Currently sending to {host}. The URL itself is never shown again.
form.urlHint: Treat it like a password: it's stored encrypted and never shown again.
form.localeHint: Messages posted to this channel are written in this language.
form.enabledHint: Turn off to pause without losing the settings.

types.label: Notifications
types.hint: Pick notification types or whole modules. Patterns like core.access-request.* also match types added later.
types.patternInvalid: Use module.entity.verb, with * as a wildcard — for example core.access-request.*

validation.name: Enter a name.
validation.url: Enter a full URL starting with https://
validation.target: This URL can't be used. Use a public https:// address — no internal or private network addresses, and no user name or password in the URL.

secret.title: Signing secret for {name}
secret.description: Your endpoint uses this secret to check that requests really come from the platform.
secret.once: Copy it now and store it safely — it won't be shown again.
secret.step1: Read the x-isbp-signature header. It looks like t=1760000000,v1=5257a8… (Unix time in seconds and the signature).
secret.step2: Compute HMAC-SHA256 with this secret over the timestamp, a dot and the raw request body (t + "." + body), as lowercase hex.
secret.step3: Accept the request only if it equals v1 (compare in constant time) and the timestamp is less than 5 minutes old.

email.title: Email (SMTP)
email.description: The mail server used for notification emails. People choose which notifications they get by email in their settings.
email.enabledHint: When off, notifications are only shown in the app and in channels.
email.tlsHint: Your mail provider's documentation says which one to use.
email.authHint: Leave both empty if the server accepts mail from this platform without signing in.
email.passwordWillRemove: The password will be removed when you save.
email.passwordHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
email.fromHint: An address, optionally with a name, such as {example}. Your server must allow sending as it.
email.enableNote: Emails start going out as soon as you save.

validation.hostRequired: Enter the SMTP server to turn email on.
validation.fromRequired: Enter the sender to turn email on.
validation.from: Enter an email address, optionally with a name, such as {example}

test.saveFirst: Save your changes first — the test uses the saved settings.
test.notReady: Turn email on and save a server and sender first.
test.title: Send a test email
test.description: Sends a short message with the saved settings, so you can check the server, sign-in and sender.
test.notConfigured: Email isn't set up yet. Turn it on and save the server and sender first.
test.failed: The mail server didn't accept the test email.
test.sent: Test email sent to {to}. It may take a minute — check the spam folder too.

log.title: Delivery log
log.intro: Every email and channel message the platform tried to send. Failed deliveries are retried a few times before they're marked as failed.
log.emptyBody: Emails and channel messages show up here with their status, so you can spot problems.
